name: Targeted Kerberoasting (Add SPN via GenericWrite)
description: Set an SPN on any user you have GenericWrite over to make them Kerberoastable, then roast and crack their hash. Clean up SPN after.

steps.label: Find GenericWrite targets via ACL enum

recommended.note: Find GenericWrite targets via ACL enumeration
Standard Kerberoasting for native SPN accounts
DCSync once cracked account is privileged

notes: Any SPN value works - it just needs to exist to enable Kerberoasting. Always clean up to avoid detection.

defense.why_it_works: If an attacker has GenericWrite or GenericAll over a user account, they can set an arbitrary SPN on that account (which doesn't already have one). This makes the account Kerberoastable - the attacker then requests a TGS for that SPN, gets the ticket encrypted with the account's NTLM hash, and cracks it offline. Useful for targeting high-privilege accounts with known weak passwords.
defense.prerequisites: GenericWrite or GenericAll ACE over the target user account (identified via BloodHound/PowerView ACL enum). Rubeus or impacket-GetUserSPNs. Target account must not already have a SPN (or must not use AES-only encryption). PowerView to set the SPN.
defense.impact: T1558.003 Kerberoasting. Converts a write ACE over a user into an offline hash crack opportunity. Particularly dangerous for accounts like help desk staff who have GenericWrite over admin accounts, or any account with a weak password and exploitable ACL path.
defense.detection:
Event 4738 (user account changed) with SPN attribute modification - an SPN suddenly appearing on a user account that didn't have one is anomalous. Event 4769 for the newly added SPN shortly after Event 4738. MDI: SPN manipulation detection. SIEM correlation: 4738 SPN change + 4769 TGS for same account in short window.
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: Event 4738: ServicePrincipalName added to user account | Event 4769: TGS request for newly added SPN | MDI: 'Suspicious SPN was added to an account' | SIEM: 4738→4769 correlation within seconds for same account
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 LDAP_Display_Name="servicePrincipalName" Operation_Type="%%14674"
| table _time, Computer, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Value

index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4769 Ticket_Encryption_Type=0x17
| stats count by Account_Name, Service_Name
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136 and AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "servicePrincipalName"
| project setTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeValue
| join kind=inner (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4769 and TicketEncryptionType == "0x17" | project roastTime=TimeGenerated, TargetUserName, ServiceName) on $left.ObjectDN == $right.TargetUserName
| where roastTime between (setTime .. (setTime + 10m))
| sort by setTime desc
defense.prevention:
Regular ACL audits to remove GenericWrite/GenericAll from non-admins over user objects. Monitor Event 4738 for unexpected SPN additions. Use long random passwords on all user accounts that could be targeted (especially DA-path accounts). Enable AES-only Kerberos on sensitive accounts.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Remove the SPN after cracking the ticket (Event 4738 shows removal but attribution is harder). Use /rc4opsec flag for the TGS request. Target accounts during low-monitoring hours.
defense.misconfiguration: Non-admin groups have GenericWrite ACEs on user objects (from legacy delegation, help desk roles). No monitoring of SPN changes on user accounts. Sensitive accounts have weak passwords.
defense.secure_config:
# Remove GenericWrite ACEs via AD ACL cleanup:
Remove-ADPermission -Identity 'DAUser1' -User 'HelpDesk' -AccessRights WriteProperty -Properties 'servicePrincipalName'

# Monitor SPN changes via Event 4738:
# SIEM: EventID=4738 AND ChangedAttributes contains 'ServicePrincipalName' AND
# TargetUserName NOT IN (known service accounts) → ALERT: possible targeted Kerberoasting

# Force AES-only on sensitive accounts:
Set-ADUser DAUser1 -KerberosEncryptionType AES256
# msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes = 16 (AES256 only) → RC4 TGS not issuable

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Check for credential dumping artifacts (LSASS access, SAM hive reads, Kerberos anomalies)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Makes an SPN-less user Kerberoastable by writing a fake SPN you can then roast:
  Set-DomainObject -Identity <user>   the user you have GenericWrite/GenericAll over
  -Set @{serviceprincipalname='nonexistent/BLAH'}   plant an arbitrary SPN
With an SPN present, Rubeus kerberoast /user:<user> returns a TGS hash; crack it (hashcat -m 13100), then clear the SPN (-Clear serviceprincipalname) to clean up.
